- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent low trend.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; increase forecast slightly to reflect sentiment-driven support.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
